prior_blocker_status: closed -- reference-style link bypass confirmed fixed via adversarial reproduction
new_blocker: angle-bracket-wrapped CommonMark reference-destination syntax ([label]: <url>) bypasses unsafe_scheme?/1: the capture group (\S+) captures the leading '<', so the extracted scheme is '<javascript' not 'javascript', failing the disallowed-scheme membership check. Reproduced for [text][ref], shorthand [text], and ![alt][ref] reference-image forms -- all bypass identically. The inline form [text](<url>) shares the same unsafe_scheme?/1 helper and is exposed to the identical bug.
required_fix: Strip a leading '<'/trailing '>' pair from the captured URL (both @markdown_link_pattern's and @markdown_reference_link_pattern's captures) before scheme extraction.
escalation: Two rounds of the same bug class (regex denylist missing a valid CommonMark syntax variant) is evidence toward design OQ-4's option (b) -- a real parser/sanitizer -- rather than continuing to patch the regex surface. Routing to REVIEWER for that determination before a third rework round, per this session's established discipline for genuine unresolved design questions.
